Loop Transit

Passenger service topology design with autonomous transfers and finite fleet.

Study 1 / 3 · Ready when you are

Three studies. Every change waits for you. Read the field guide, then explore the machine.

Begin study

Undo action
Reset study

FIELD GUIDE

How the machine works
Draw cyclic train lines over the visible physical track, then allocate the finite train fleet. Repeated stations allow integrated branch detours; two-station shuttles are also valid. Each train holds two riders.
Advance one pulse to add scheduled demand, move each train one edge, alight riders and board waiting passengers following a shortest service route. Transferring riders cannot board again until the next pulse. Actual onboard destinations, queues and train positions remain visible.
Deliver the quota before closing without overflowing a platform. Empty lines can be replaced freely; removing an occupied line spends the one relocation token and returns its riders to their current station. The final study includes a public track closure/opening requiring service redesign.

Tap any labeled control, or use Tab then Enter / Space. There is no timer. Selection does not spend a turn. Symbols and numbers always accompany color.

Study 1 / 3 · Connect the branch

Pulse 0/20 · delivered 0/6 · trains 0/2 · lines 0/2. Each train carries 2. Platform limit 3.

Physical track edges: A—B, B—C, C—D, D—A, C—E

Build a directed cyclic line by selecting neighboring stations in order. Last must connect to first; a two-station shuttle is allowed. Stations may repeat in a line (up to ten stops), allowing an integrated branch detour. Add a train to the line. Each pulse adds scheduled passengers, then moves each train one edge, lets riders alight/transfer, and boards passengers whose shortest service route follows its next edge. Transfer riders wait until the following pulse before boarding again. Nothing moves while editing.
